title: Integration of Experimental and Predicted Structural Tools to Understand Ribosome-Associated Quality Control
content: Ribosome stalling leads to the accumulation of defective nascent polypeptides, which can cause proteotoxic stress if left unresolved. The ribosome-associated quality control (RQC) complex mitigates this challenge by ubiquitinating and extracting stalled polypeptides for degradation [1-3]. In eukaryotes, the RQC complex consists of Ltn1, an E3 ubiquitin ligase that mediates K48-linked polyubiquitination; Rqc2, which facilitates elongation of stalled nascent chains with CAT tails; Rqc1, a factor with a poorly understood role in ubiquitination; and the Cdc48-Ufd1-Npl4 ATPase complex, which extracts ubiquitylated substrates for degradation [4-6]. While previous studies have defined individual components of the RQC pathway, the precise mechanism of stalled nascent chain extraction remains incompletely understood. Here, we present a comprehensive structural analysis of the RQC complex using single-particle cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) and AlphaFold 3 structure prediction to resolve these mechanistic details [7].
